audits.standard: Best practice: at least annual HbA1c and prolactin for all; vitamin D only if symptomatic of deficiency
audits.setting: Five in-patient secure wards (medium and low secure, including Northside House)

cycle1.result: 100% tested on the medium secure unit, but vitamin D tested without documented clinical indication; on the other units prolactin and HbA1c were least measured (18% male LSU, 23% female ward); vitamin D testing 38% female ward and 18% male ward.

audits.title: Monitoring Matters: Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People Prescribed Antipsychotics in Community CAMHS
audits.standard: Community CAMHS Physical Health Standard Operating Procedure for antipsychotic monitoring
audits.setting: Centenary House community CAMHS, Sheffield

cycle1.result: Blood tests 77% (10/13); ECG 85% (11/13); height and weight 62% (8/13); blood pressure and heart rate 62% (8/13); allergy status 62% (8/13); neurological examination for EPSEs 0%; only 6 patients had all parameters documented

audits.intervention: Proposed electronic reminders, structured antipsychotic monitoring template, teaching for medical staff and re-audit in 6 to 12 months
audits.other_findings: Prolactin monitoring was absent in the single patient prescribed risperidone.
audits.citation: Marlow G. Monitoring Matters: Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People Prescribed Antipsychotics in Community CAMHS. BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S248-S248.
